title: Scripture and Discernment
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Scripture and discernment teaches that God’s Word trains believers to recognize truth, reject error, test spiritual claims, and walk wisely before the Lord. Discernment is not suspicion or pride; it is truth-shaped judgment under Scripture.
summary: Scripture and discernment teaches that God’s Word trains believers to recognize truth, reject error, test spiritual claims, and walk wisely before the Lord. Discernment is not suspicion or pride; it is truth-shaped judgment under Scripture.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the truth, and Scripture teaches believers to recognize what accords with Him. True discernment protects devotion to Christ and guards believers from deception that would draw them away from the Gospel.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Believers are called to discernment because not every voice, teaching, spirit, experience, or claim is from God. Scripture gives God’s people a trustworthy standard by which truth and error must be tested.

Discernment begins with God’s Word. Scripture exposes the thoughts and intentions of the heart, reveals God’s truth, and trains believers to distinguish what is faithful from what is false. Human emotion, popularity, charisma, spiritual language, or impressive experiences are not enough.

The Bereans were commended because they examined the Scriptures to test what they heard. This kind of discernment is not rebellion against good teaching; it is faithfulness to God. Teachers, movements, prophecies, counsel, habits, and desires must all be brought under Scripture.

True discernment is humble and Christ-centered. It does not create arrogant fault-finding or fearful suspicion. It produces wisdom, holiness, love for truth, protection from deception, and deeper faithfulness to Jesus.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers are vulnerable to deception because false teaching often uses biblical words, emotional stories, spiritual claims, or promises of breakthrough. Without Scripture-shaped discernment, people can be manipulated, confused, or pulled away from Christ while thinking they are being spiritual.

This doctrine is especially important for the wounded, desperate, or spiritually hungry. Pain can make people vulnerable to any voice that promises quick answers. Scripture gives them a faithful standard so they can test what they hear and remain anchored in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Test what you hear by Scripture. Do not accept teaching merely because it is popular, emotional, supernatural-sounding, or attached to a trusted personality. Ask whether it honors Christ, agrees with the Gospel, fits the whole counsel of God, and produces faithful obedience. Seek discernment with humility, prayer, and love for truth.
